note: Hand-labelled sample answers. `labels` is the expected verdict of each LLM grader of `case`; regex graders are deterministic.

samples.label: good
samples.answer: I do not take the author's word. An empty two-dot range only says no commit is reachable from the right side and not the left, so it does not establish ancestry. I run `git merge-base --is-ancestor <base> <integration-head>` and read the exit status, then `git rev-list --count <base>..<integration-head>` to see how far behind it is. The brief then carries an id, the whole task, the integration branch, the verified base commit, the owned files, the skills, a finish line, a stopping condition, whether a GPU is granted, and the Needs you / Changed / Found shape. The last commit must carry `Brief: <id> done` or `Brief: <id> blocked: <question>`; the message is the notification and git is the record.

samples.label: bad
samples.answer: The author says the base is on the integration branch and the range is empty, so I accept it and send the brief with the task and the branch name. Replies are fine as chat messages.

samples.answer: Not yet. I read the lane's commit messages for owed legs, and one says a counters re-record is owed. That leg runs on the lane's head with the integration head merged in first, under a GPU grant and one GPU leg at a time. I hold the landing until it has run, and the re-recorded ledger lands with the lane, with the reason for the move in the commit message.

samples.label: good
samples.answer: I do not accept the reclassification on the peer's say-so. I check the reported defect against the current files first. Then I rule on it as a scoped fix, a recorded open item or a dismissal with its reason. A real defect is fixed or recorded; renaming its severity does not hide it. Whatever I rule, the finding gets a lane or a named deferral before I set it aside.

samples.label: bad
samples.answer: The peer knows its lane best, so I mark the finding as a nit and let the lane land.

samples.answer: No. The message is only the notification; git is the record. I check that the last commit carries `Brief: L7 done` or a blocked trailer and ask the lane to add it. Then I inspect the reported changes and the checks, following the verification skill, before I merge anything.

samples.label: good
samples.answer: Busy is not progress, so I do not queue filler to look busy. I plan backward from the milestone's critical path, find the least-prepared item on it, and put the best-fit partner there. The small cleanups stay unqueued.

samples.label: bad
samples.answer: I hand the idle partners the cleanups at once so everyone is visibly working.

samples.label: good
samples.answer: I allocate by the machine's fixed capability (CPU class, GPU, RAM, OS, network), mapped once and checked every turn. A load governor admits queued work on measured spare CPU and free RAM and holds it under memory pressure. At about 7 GB a run, two full World test runs never run at once on a 32 GB box. The GPU leg starts on a GPU-idle transition. Every build uses -nodeReuse:false.

samples.label: bad
samples.answer: All five agents start their builds now and the GPU leg runs whenever it is ready; more parallelism finishes sooner.
